## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Kilocode skill cache poison via gray-matter (SMALL ~1-2h, tools)

- **What**: Kilocode PR #14777 (merged 2026-10-04 as commit `b0aeda5`) fixes gray-matter cache dropping project skills after YAML parse errors. gray-matter caches each input string before parsing; when strict YAML throws (e.g. unquoted colon in `description`), cache keeps entry with empty `data`, so every later parse of same content returns no `name` and skill is silently skipped. In `kilo serve` with worktree + primary checkout sharing identical SKILL.md files, every directory after first loses those skills. Fix: pass `{ cache: null }` to `matter()` so it bypasses cache. Alexi has identical vulnerability in three modules: `src/skill/index.ts` L133 `matter(content)` (no options), `src/agent/customAgentLoader.ts` L?? `matter(content)`, `src/command/index.ts` L?? `matter(content)` (confirmed via `grep -r "matter\(" src/`). One malformed skill/agent/command YAML poisons cache for all subsequent identical files in same process. Multi-worktree setups (`alexi agent` equivalent to `kilo serve`) lose skills after first parse error.

- **Why**: Alexi skill system (`src/skill/index.ts` 679 lines), custom agent loader (`src/agent/customAgentLoader.ts`), and command loader (`src/command/index.ts`) all use `gray-matter` package (v4.0.3 in `package.json`) for frontmatter parsing. None pass cache-bypass option. Pattern: `const { data, content: promptContent } = matter(content);` (skill L133). Kilocode commit message says "gray-matter caches each input string before parsing" + "Pass options to matter() so it bypasses the cache". Alexi TUI long-running process can parse same skill multiple times (reload, worktrees). One YAML error (unquoted colon common in AI-written descriptions) breaks all future parses of that content. Fix is one-line per call site: `matter(content, { cache: null })` instead of `matter(content)`. Test: create skill with malformed YAML, parse it (error + cache poison), parse valid skill with identical content (silently returns empty `data` without fix, works with fix). SMALL ~1-2h: update three `matter()` calls (skill, agent, command loaders) to pass `{ cache: null }`, add unit test in `src/skill/__tests__/` or existing test file for malformed YAML followed by valid skill with same content, verify skill parsed correctly second time, verify `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` green.

- **Source**: https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/pull/14777 (Kilocode skill cache fix, merged 2026-10-04), https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode/commit/b0aeda5 (fix commit), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/skill/index.ts L133 (Alexi `matter(content)` without options), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/package.json (gray-matter v4.0.3), `grep -r "matter\(" src/` (three call sites confirmed: skill, agent, command)

- **Category**: tools (skill loader, agent loader, command loader, gray-matter cache bypass)

- **Size**: SMALL ~1-2h (update `matter(content)` to `matter(content, { cache: null })` in three files: `src/skill/index.ts` L133, `src/agent/customAgentLoader.ts` L?? (grep exact line), `src/command/index.ts` L?? (grep exact line), add unit test in existing test file or `src/skill/__tests__/skill-cache.test.ts` for malformed YAML followed by valid skill, assert valid skill parses correctly, verify `npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test` green, test in running TUI with malformed skill + reload)

#### 5. Claude Code batch git diff performance pattern (REFERENCE, not immediate CLI work)

- **What**: Claude Code PR #98445 (merged 2026-09-30 as commit `292c5b8`) optimizes diff pane to read every file's hunks with one git process instead of one process per file. Commit title: "diff: the pane reads every file's hunks with one git process, where it started one per file". Pattern: when displaying diffs for multiple files, spawn single `git diff` with all paths as arguments instead of N individual `git diff <path>` subprocesses. Reduces process overhead, file descriptor churn, git repo lock contention. Claude Code diff pane had file-per-process pattern, changed to batch.

- **Why**: Alexi CLI has `src/tool/tools/bash.ts` (25753 bytes), `src/tool/tools/apply-patch.ts` (16917 bytes), check if any git diff commands iterate files instead of batching. Grepping `git diff` usage (not done yet) would show if Alexi spawns multiple git processes for multi-file diffs. If yes, batching pattern applies (SMALL ~2-3h: refactor to batch paths). If no (single `git diff` with multiple paths already, or no multi-file diff iteration), pattern is informational only. Claude Code context: diff pane is UI feature, Alexi has no diff pane. But bash tool or apply-patch tool may iterate git diff. **Marking REFERENCE not NEW actionable** - needs grep to confirm Alexi has multi-file diff iteration bottleneck. Not adding to backlog today, revisit if git diff performance issue surfaces.

- **Source**: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/pull/98445 (batch git diff), https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/commit/292c5b8 (commit), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/tools/bash.ts (25753 bytes), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/tool/tools/apply-patch.ts (16917 bytes)

- **Category**: REFERENCE (performance pattern, git subprocess batching)

- **Size**: REFERENCE. Not actionable until git diff iteration bottleneck confirmed in Alexi. If confirmed, SMALL ~2-3h (refactor git diff calls to batch paths instead of iterate).

#### 6. Claude Code permission hierarchy (REFERENCE, not immediate CLI work)

- **What**: Claude Code PRs #98080 + #98083 (merged 2026-09-29) refine permission system: (1) settings deny rule holds over allow/ask from user-installed plugin (#98080), (2) allowManagedModsOnly flag prevents user-installed mods from loading (#98083). Pattern: explicit deny in settings config (admin/org level) takes precedence over allow/ask from user-installed extension (user level). Before: user plugin allow could override settings deny. After: deny is absolute. Separate flag `allowManagedModsOnly` (settings-level) blocks all user-installed mods from loading if enabled, regardless of their individual permissions.

- **Why**: Alexi CLI has permission system (`src/permission/` 6 modules), check if deny rules hold over user-level allow already, or if user rules can override deny. Claude Code pattern: three-tier hierarchy (org/admin settings > user-installed plugin > defaults), deny at higher tier blocks lower tier allow. Alexi permission policy (`src/permission/policy.ts` likely has precedence rules). If Alexi already has deny-wins precedence, pattern is informational. If not, consider adding (MEDIUM ~4-6h: audit permission resolution, add deny precedence, test user allow cannot override settings deny). **Marking REFERENCE not NEW actionable** - needs audit of `src/permission/` to confirm Alexi lacks deny precedence. Not adding to backlog today, revisit if permission bypass issue surfaces.

- **Source**: https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/pull/98080 (deny precedence), https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/pull/98083 (allowManagedModsOnly), https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/commit/16da1ec (deny commit), https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/commit/0d7f14d (managed-only commit), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/permission/ (6 modules)

- **Category**: REFERENCE (permission hierarchy, deny precedence, managed-only mode)

- **Size**: REFERENCE. Not actionable until Alexi permission bypass confirmed. If confirmed, MEDIUM ~4-6h (audit permission resolution in `src/permission/policy.ts`, add deny-wins precedence rule, add allowManagedModsOnly config flag, test user allow cannot override settings deny, test managed-only mode blocks user installs).
